Configure sex chromosome mapping

Source: R/ggwas-package.R
set_sex_chr_map.Rd

ggwas stores chromosomes as integer codes. By default it uses human conventions, where chromosome 23 is labeled "X", 24 is "Y", 25 is "XY" and 26 is "MT". For other organisms, pass the genome's Seqinfo object (GenomeInfoDb) and the codes are taken from its sequence names: numbered chromosomes keep their number, and named ones (X, Y, Z, W, MT, ...) are numbered after the last autosome, in Seqinfo order. Unplaced scaffolds are ignored.

Usage

set_sex_chr_map(map = .default_sex_chr_map)

Arguments

map

A Seqinfo object, or any object that has one (TxDb, EnsDb, BSgenome); or a named integer vector mapping labels to integers, e.g. c(X = 20L, Y = 21L). Pass NULL to disable the mapping (chromosomes displayed as plain numbers).

Value

The previous mapping (invisibly).

Examples

# Mouse (GRCm39): 19 autosomes, then X, Y and MT
mouse <- GenomeInfoDb::Seqinfo(c(1:19, "X", "Y", "MT"), genome = "GRCm39")
old <- set_sex_chr_map(mouse)
getOption("ggwas.sex_chr_map")
#>  X  Y MT 
#> 20 21 22 

# Chicken: Z and W follow the last numbered chromosome
chicken <- GenomeInfoDb::Seqinfo(c(1:39, "Z", "W", "MT"))
set_sex_chr_map(chicken)

# Disable: all chromosomes shown as numbers
set_sex_chr_map(NULL)

# Restore the previous (here the human default) mapping
set_sex_chr_map(old)
